key_insight: The paper shows that generating related user intents can expand e-commerce search recall beyond exact matches, improving discovery of substitutes and complementary items without sacrificing relevance.
engineering_relevance: A two-stage LLM-to-SLM architecture makes discovery-augmented search more deployable by balancing quality, latency, and cost for large-scale marketplace search.
method: Use closed-weight LLMs to generate implicit related intents for head queries.
Train a smaller SLM with LoRA adapters and teacher-student distillation to generalize discovery to tail queries.
Fuse intent-conditioned recall expansion into a hybrid search pipeline for scalable candidate generation.
evidence_signal: The authors validate intent quality with LLM-as-a-judge checks against human preferences and measure downstream impact with end-to-end session-level purchase analysis, reporting coverage growth from about 60% to 80% of query traffic at roughly 30% of teacher inference cost.
watch_item: Generative recall expansion can introduce relevance drift or bias toward commercially salient items, so careful online monitoring and guardrails are needed before deployment.
paper_title: Improving Item Discoverability in e-Commerce Search via Related Intent Generation
